A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Walrus study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining, downstream finetuning, cross-domain comparisons, and ablations, including Section 5 and appendix Tables 3, 7, and 8.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds context-length experiments, inference measurements, and trajectory-distribution evaluations in Appendices E and F.

M1.justification: The architecture, prediction objective, patch jittering, adaptive tokenization, augmentations, sampling strategy, and finetuning adaptations remain the same. Expanded encoder explanations and sampling pseudocode document existing components rather than establish a new modeling or training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same 19 pretraining datasets, eight downstream datasets, and synthetic missing-parameter advection example. The new context-length sweep and distributional measurements concern retained tasks; they do not establish additional dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain MPP-AViT-L, Poseidon-L, and DPOT-H, with DPOT-H serving as the 3D comparator. HalfWalrus, Naive, and Scratch remain in the diversity experiment. The added advection controls vary Walrus's context length rather than introduce another external baseline.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation beyond pointwise VRMSE with full-rollout spatially averaged temporal W1 across downstream and pretraining tasks. Appendix E adds context-length controls and inference benchmarking, and revises the stated advection equation and parameter ranges. Figure 4 now specifies a 3D prediction start of T=11, whereas v1 states T=17 universally; v2's prose still repeats T=17. These establish changes in reported protocols, without establishing which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The jitter, absolute-position-embedding, and pretraining-diversity ablations are retained. v2 adds a focused history-length ablation on the existing advection example, testing whether history explains the advantage over Poseidon, plus corresponding timing measurements (Figure 12 and Table 8). The earlier composite visualization containing the RSG qualitative example is removed.

E5.justification: v1 already reports standard-deviation bands and uncertainty in the APE ablation. v2 additionally supplies within-dataset standard deviations for aggregate VRMSE tables and identifies unavailable trajectory-level spread for PNS. The timing experiment specifies 10 warmup and 20 timed passes with variability. No increase in independent training runs or seeds is established.

E6.justification: Tables 12 and 16 add extensive W1 results, including PNS scores favoring DPOT-H (0.0613) over Walrus (0.2244). Figure 12 adds advection VRMSE of 0.183 with six history frames versus 1.269 with one; Table 8 adds timings. Most original VRMSE results remain unchanged, but some expanded tables differ: DPOT-H's Staircase one-step score is 0.0021 in v2 Table 13 versus 0.0017 in v1 Table 1. v2's main Table 1 still retains 0.0017.

T1.justification: The alias-cancellation result is retained, but v2 Appendix A.1 revises its mathematical justification: it explicitly evaluates the oscillatory integral instead of invoking the Cauchy integral theorem. It also qualifies Fourier normalization factors and adds the O(1/T) Monte Carlo convergence statement. Merely relabeling the existing derivation as a lemma and proposition is not a separate theoretical advance.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the claimed jitter success rate from 89% to 84%, corresponding to 17/19 versus 16/19 scenarios; Appendix A.1.3 explains the exclusion of MHD's unusably large errors. The principal architecture, transfer, diversity, and 56/65-metric claims remain. The appendix also retains an inconsistent older 89% sentence.

C2.justification: Appendix E more explicitly attributes the advection advantage to history rather than backbone architecture and discusses runtime costs and model-size confounding. Section 5 and Appendix F add qualifications about W1's temporal permutation invariance, inability to assess coherent structures, and limited ergodicity, alongside reasons for omitting physics-specific metrics. Existing RSG/PNS scientific-validity limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds topology-aware sampling pseudocode, expands the hMLP description, and repairs undefined or incorrect variables in the patch-jitter pseudocode. It newly documents PNS boundary handling and 66-to-64 interpolation, RSG's retained time stride of five, and VRMSE epsilon of 10^-7. These are additional implementation disclosures, not demonstrated changes to the underlying experiments. Code and weight access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Caflisch on Monte Carlo methods, Molinaro et al. on distributional evaluation, and Liu et al. on Swin. The shortened background removes several broader references, including Ruiz et al. on memory. Positioning relative to the principal physics foundation models remains stable; publication and title updates to retained works are not new research relationships.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, distributed-training explanation, experimental discussion, and conclusion are extensively condensed or rewritten. A new Appendix A collects derivations and extended explanations previously distributed through the paper, subsequent appendices are reorganized, and an impact statement is added. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main paper to a two-column layout, merges v1 Figures 6 and 7 into Figure 4, relocates jitter and pretraining plots, and removes the composite 3D visualization. It splits downstream result tables, adds expanded uncertainty tables, introduces the context-length figure and timing/W1 tables, and resizes and redistributes appendix visualizations.

improvement.justification: The controlled history experiment strengthens the explanation of the advection results, while W1 evaluations provide useful evidence beyond pointwise errors, including baseline wins. Clearer mathematical reasoning and implementation disclosures also improve transparency. These gains are limited by unresolved reporting conflicts: some new appendix scores disagree with the retained main table, and jitter success rates and sample counts remain inconsistent. The additions improve the paper, but do not constitute a comprehensive repair of its evaluation and reporting limitations.
